entries.title: Tell HN: YC will help you find a co-founder
entries.author: kcorbitt
entries.current_title: Tell HN: YC will help you find a co-founder
entries.excerpt: Hey HN, I’m Kyle Corbitt, and I work on Startup School ( https://www.startupschool.org/ ), YC’s free program to help people learn how to start a startup. Today we’re launching a new major feature: co-founder matching ( https://www.startupschool.org/cofounder-matching ). Interested founders can create a profile, input their requirements (location, time commitment, skills, etc) and quickly review screened candidates. We don’t charge for this or take any equity in the teams form
entries.guide_zh: YC Startup School 介绍寻找联合创始人的服务，帮助创业者建立合作。

entries.title: Tell HN: Coming soon – “Meet the Batch” threads for parallel Launch HNs
entries.author: dang
entries.current_title: Tell HN: Coming soon – “Meet the Batch” threads for parallel Launch HNs
entries.excerpt: Each YC startup gets one chance to do a Launch HN thread that gets placed on HN's front page [1]. This is one of the three things that HN gives back to YC in exchange for funding it [2]. We started doing these in 2017 and they've worked out pretty well over the years [3], I think mostly because they're more interesting than job ads. entries.title: Tell HN: Consider listing your contact details
entries.author: cpach
entries.current_title: Tell HN: Consider listing your contact details
entries.excerpt: TL;DR: Consider listing your contact details in your HN profile! There are lots of interesting conversations happening here on HN. But sometimes people might want to continue the discussions even after threads fall of the front page. Have you considered listing your contact details on HN so that people can get in touch with you more easily? If you want to do that, please note that it’s not enough to fill in the email field on your profile. Only the HN admins can see that fiel

entries.title: Ask HN: Do you have a process or a framework to learn specific skills quickly?
entries.author: hypnotist
entries.current_title: Ask HN: Do you have a process or a framework to learn specific skills quickly?
entries.excerpt: Any suggestions/ frameworks on how to learn specific skill, retain the knowledge and be able to share it(in for ex. written form) I usually jump in straight away and start learning "on the job" but I realised that I forget too much and i do not have any notes to refer to later on. Examples of specific skill: - How to write a good cold email - how to learn some snowboarding trick - how to store your bitcoin safely etc.
entries.guide_zh: 有没有可复用的快速学习框架，既学会技能，又记得住、讲得清？
